results.question: How many employees are there?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees;

results.question: How many projects have status 'active'?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS active_projects FROM projects WHERE status = 'active';

results.question: List the names of all clients in Denmark in alphabetical order.
results.sql: SELECT name FROM clients WHERE country = 'Denmark' ORDER BY name ASC;

results.question: What is the total budget across all projects?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(budget) AS total_budget FROM projects;

results.question: How many invoices are overdue?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS overdue_invoices FROM invoices WHERE status = 'overdue'

results.question: How many expenses are in the Travel category?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS travel_expense_count FROM expenses WHERE category = 'Travel';

results.question: How many employees work in each office?
results.sql: SELECT office, COUNT(*) AS employee_count FROM employees GROUP BY office ORDER BY employee_count DESC;

results.question: What is the largest single expense amount?
results.sql: SELECT MAX(amount) AS largest_expense FROM expenses;

results.question: Which client has the highest total project budget? Give the client name.
results.sql: SELECT c.name FROM clients c JOIN projects p ON p.client_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY SUM(p.budget) DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: What is the total invoiced amount per client, highest first? Include every client that has been invoiced.
results.sql: SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(i.amount) AS total_invoiced FROM clients c JOIN projects p ON p.client_id = c.id JOIN invoices i ON i.project_id = p.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_invoiced DESC

results.question: How many hours have been logged in total on project 1?
results.sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(hours), 0) AS total_hours FROM timesheets WHERE project_id = 1;

results.question: Which 5 employees have logged the most billable hours? Give their names and the hours.
results.sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(t.hours) AS billable_hours FROM timesheets t JOIN employees e ON e.id = t.employee_id WHERE t.billable = 1 GROUP BY e.id, e.name ORDER BY billable_hours DESC LIMIT 5;

results.question: What is the total amount of expenses per category?
results.sql: SELECT category, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM expenses GROUP BY category ORDER BY total_amount DESC;

results.question: Which employees lead more than 3 projects? Give their names.
results.sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN projects p ON p.lead_id = e.id GROUP BY e.id, e.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 3

results.question: What is the average amount of the paid invoices?
results.sql: SELECT AVG(amount) AS avg_paid_invoice_amount FROM invoices WHERE status = 'paid'

results.question: Which clients have no overdue invoices? Give the client names.
results.sql: SELECT c.name FROM clients c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects p JOIN invoices i ON i.project_id = p.id WHERE p.client_id = c.id AND i.status = 'overdue') ORDER BY c.name

results.question: How many different employees have logged time on active projects?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.employee_id) AS employee_count FROM timesheets t JOIN projects p ON p.id = t.project_id WHERE p.status = 'active';

results.question: What is the total unpaid invoice amount (invoices that are not paid) per client country?
results.sql: SELECT c.country, SUM(i.amount) AS total_unpaid FROM invoices i JOIN projects p ON i.project_id = p.id JOIN clients c ON p.client_id = c.id WHERE i.status <> 'paid' GROUP BY c.country ORDER BY total_unpaid DESC

results.question: Which projects have been invoiced for more than their budget? Give the project name, total invoiced and budget.
results.sql: SELECT p.name AS project_name, SUM(i.amount) AS total_invoiced, p.budget AS budget FROM projects p JOIN invoices i ON i.project_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name, p.budget HAVING SUM(i.amount) > p.budget ORDER BY SUM(i.amount) - p.budget DESC

results.question: How many invoices were issued in each year?
results.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', issue_date) AS year, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM invoices GROUP BY year ORDER BY year

results.question: Which employee logged the most hours in March 2026? Give the name.
results.sql: SELECT e.name FROM timesheets t JOIN employees e ON e.id = t.employee_id WHERE t.work_date >= '2026-03-01' AND t.work_date < '2026-04-01' GROUP BY e.id, e.name ORDER BY SUM(t.hours) DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: What percentage of all logged hours are billable? Round to 1 decimal place.
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN billable = 1 THEN hours ELSE 0 END) / SUM(hours), 1) AS billable_pct FROM timesheets;

results.question: On average, how many days pass between the issue date and the paid date of paid invoices? Round to 1 decimal place.
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(paid_date) - julianday(issue_date)), 1) AS avg_days_to_pay FROM invoices WHERE status = 'paid' AND paid_date IS NOT NULL;

results.question: Which clients have at least one overdue invoice? Give the client names.
results.sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.name FROM clients c JOIN projects p ON p.client_id = c.id JOIN invoices i ON i.project_id = p.id WHERE i.status = 'overdue' ORDER BY c.name

results.question: For each project lead, what is the combined budget of the projects they lead? Show the top 3 leads by name.
results.sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(p.budget) AS total_budget FROM projects p JOIN employees e ON e.id = p.lead_id GROUP BY e.id, e.name ORDER BY total_budget DESC LIMIT 3

results.question: Which employee has the highest total expenses? Give the name and the total.
results.sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(x.amount) AS total_expenses FROM expenses x JOIN employees e ON e.id = x.employee_id GROUP BY e.id, e.name ORDER BY total_expenses DESC LIMIT 1

results.question: Which month had the highest total invoiced amount? Give the month as YYYY-MM and the total.
results.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', issue_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total FROM invoices GROUP BY month ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 1;

results.question: How many projects have both an overdue invoice and an expense above 4000?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS project_count FROM projects p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoices i WHERE i.project_id = p.id AND i.status = 'overdue') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM expenses e WHERE e.project_id = p.id AND e.amount > 4000)
